from.place: comparison isomorphism for perfect complexes: identify RHom(K,M) with M tensor^L RHom(K,O_X), and transport the dual through derived pullback

title: Derived tensor-Hom comparison for a perfect complex
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let K be a perfect complex [def-pc-perfect-complex] in D_QCoh(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category], and let M be a quasi-coherent complex. Define K^\vee := R\mathcal Hom_{O_X}(K,O_X) [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then K^\vee is a perfect complex in D_QCoh(O_X). Use the tensor-internal-Hom adjunction and the symmetry of the derived tensor product [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] of [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-adjunction]; for objects A,E of D(O_X) let \mathrm{ev}:R\mathcal Hom_{O_X}(A,E)\otimes^L A\to E be the evaluation map, the map corresponding to \mathrm{id}_{R\mathcal Hom(A,E)} under that adjunction, and put \epsilon:=\mathrm{ev}:K^\vee\otimes^L K\to O_X. Define the canonical global map M\otimes^L K^\vee \longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_{O_X}(K,M) to be the map corresponding under the adjunction to 1_M\otimes\epsilon:M\otimes^L K^\vee\otimes^L K\to M\otimes^L O_X=M; this map is an isomorphism. Define the canonical bidual map K\longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_{O_X}(K^\vee,O_X) as the map corresponding under the adjunction to the composite K\otimes^L K^\vee\cong K^\vee\otimes^L K\xrightarrow{\epsilon}O_X of the symmetry isomorphism with \epsilon; it is an isomorphism. Let \eta:O_X\to K\otimes^L K^\vee be the unique map whose composite with the isomorphism K\otimes^L K^\vee\cong R\mathcal Hom_{O_X}(K,K) (the case M=K) is the map O_X\to R\mathcal Hom_{O_X}(K,K) corresponding under the adjunction to O_X\otimes^L K=K\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}_K}K; then (\epsilon,\eta) satisfy the two zig-zag identities (1_K\otimes\epsilon)\circ(\eta\otimes 1_K)=\mathrm{id}_K and (\epsilon\otimes 1_{K^\vee})\circ(1_{K^\vee}\otimes\eta)=\mathrm{id}_{K^\vee}, so (K,K^\vee,\epsilon,\eta) is an exact pairing in D_QCoh(O_X) with its derived tensor product. For every morphism of schemes g:X'\to X, with derived pullback Lg^* [def-pc-derived-pullback] and Lg^*O_X=O_{X'}, define the canonical base-change map Lg^*K^\vee \longrightarrow R\mathcal Hom_{O_{X'}}(Lg^*K,O_{X'}) as the map corresponding under the adjunction on X' to the composite Lg^*K^\vee\otimes^L Lg^*K\cong Lg^*(K^\vee\otimes^L K)\xrightarrow{Lg^*\epsilon}O_{X'} of the isomorphism of [lem-pc-derived-pullback-tensor-product] with Lg^*\epsilon; it is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Local computation, for an arbitrary object M of D(O_X). By [def-pc-perfect-complex] there is an affine open cover X=\bigcup U_i with K|_{U_i}\cong\mathcal E^\bullet, a strictly perfect complex (bounded, each term a direct summand of a finite free O_{U_i}-module). Fix such U=U_i and represent M|_U by a complex \mathcal F^\bullet. By [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-restrict-open], K^\vee|_U\cong R\mathcal Hom_{O_U}(\mathcal E^\bullet,O_U) and R\mathcal Hom_{O_X}(K,M)|_U\cong R\mathcal Hom_{O_U}(\mathcal E^\bullet,\mathcal F^\bullet), and by [lem-pc-rhom-strict-perfect-hom] these are the Hom complexes \mathcal E^{\vee\bullet}=\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal E^\bullet,O_U), with terms \mathcal Hom(\mathcal E^{-n},O_U), and \mathcal Hom^\bullet(\mathcal E^\bullet,\mathcal F^\bullet). The terms of \mathcal E^{\vee\bullet} are again direct summands of finite free modules, so \mathcal E^{\vee\bullet} is strictly perfect (hence K^\vee is perfect) and has quasi-coherent terms (hence quasi-coherent cohomology sheaves on U; quasi-coherence of cohomology is local, so K^\vee\in D_QCoh(O_X)). Being bounded with flat terms, \mathcal E^{\vee\bullet} is K-flat by [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat], so with the symmetry of [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-adjunction] M|_U\otimes^L K^\vee|_U is represented by \operatorname{Tot}(\mathcal F^\bullet\otimes\mathcal E^{\vee\bullet}) [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. On these representatives the map of the statement (defined by the adjunction, whose formation commutes with restriction to U because restriction is termwise on tensor products and commutes with R\mathcal Hom) is the termwise map \mathcal F^p\otimes\mathcal Hom(\mathcal E^{-q},O_U)\to\mathcal Hom(\mathcal E^{-q},\mathcal F^p), as in Tag 08DQ; this is an isomorphism of sheaves for \mathcal E^{-q} finite free (both sides are (\mathcal F^p)^{\oplus r}) and hence for a direct summand of a finite free module. Likewise the bidual map on U is the termwise map \mathcal E^n\to\mathcal Hom(\mathcal Hom(\mathcal E^n,O_U),O_U) (use [lem-pc-rhom-strict-perfect-hom] for the strictly perfect \mathcal E^{\vee\bullet}), an isomorphism for the same reason.

Globalization of the isomorphisms. The evaluation map M\otimes^L K^\vee\to R\mathcal Hom_{O_X}(K,M) and the bidual map are globally defined morphisms of D(O_X) (by the adjunction in the statement), and by Step 1 their restrictions to every U_i are isomorphisms. A morphism of D(O_X) is an isomorphism if and only if it induces isomorphisms on all cohomology sheaves, which can be checked on an open cover; hence both are isomorphisms. No morphism is glued here: only the property of being an isomorphism is checked locally. In particular the evaluation map is an isomorphism for every object M of D(O_X), not only for quasi-coherent M.

Zig-zag identities. Apply [lem-pc-dualizable-evaluation-criterion] with D=K^\vee and e=\epsilon: its hypothesis, that for every object M of D(O_X) the map M\otimes^L K^\vee\to R\mathcal Hom_{O_X}(K,M) corresponding under [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-adjunction] to 1_M\otimes\epsilon is an isomorphism, is Step 2, and its coevaluation is the \eta of the statement (the case M=K). It gives both triangle identities.

Base change. Let g:X'\to X and U=U_i as in Step 1, and cover g^{-1}(U) by affine opens V. The complexes \mathcal E^\bullet and \mathcal E^{\vee\bullet} are bounded with flat terms, so by [lem-pc-flat-complex-derived-pullback] (applied to g|_V:V\to U) (Lg^*K)|_V and (Lg^*K^\vee)|_V are represented by the termwise pullbacks g^*\mathcal E^\bullet and g^*\mathcal E^{\vee\bullet}; the former is strictly perfect, so by [lem-sc-derived-internal-hom-restrict-open] and [lem-pc-rhom-strict-perfect-hom] R\mathcal Hom_{O_{X'}}(Lg^*K,O_{X'})|_V is the Hom complex \mathcal Hom^\bullet(g^*\mathcal E^\bullet,O_V). Computing the isomorphism of [lem-pc-derived-pullback-tensor-product] on these flat representatives, the base-change map of the statement is on V the termwise map g^*\mathcal Hom(\mathcal E^{-n},O_U)\to\mathcal Hom(g^*\mathcal E^{-n},O_V), which is an isomorphism for a finite free module and hence for a direct summand of one (Tag 0GM7, proof of (1)). Being an isomorphism is checked on cohomology sheaves, locally on X', as in Step 2.
